accepted_deliverable_row.Name: Proposal, validation and outcome contract
accepted_deliverable_row.Description: Specify the same host validation/application path and truthful proposal lifecycle for all actors while domain truth and accepted results remain host-owned. Interfaces: Consumes DEL-03-01 basis/catalog and PKG-04 autonomy/act distinctions; DEL-03-03 external receiving uses this path; host views show old/new values and receipts. Verification: Stale proposals refuse with a reason, later selection cannot retarget, duplicate submission has one effect and unknown outcomes remain unknown; success or queued status never substitutes for actual human acceptance.
accepted_deliverable_row.ResponsibleParty: App/shared operation-contract owner; host owner owns validation/application/receipts/UI
accepted_deliverable_row.AnticipatedArtifacts: CONFIG: proposal/basis/origin/outcome schemas;DOC: proposal lifecycle and shared validation route;TEST: stale, retarget, duplicate and unknown-outcome contract fixtures
accepted_deliverable_row.ContextEnvelopeNotes: One bounded behavior or contract slice; named interfaces and focused checks constrain required context. File counts remain production-definition estimates, not model limits.
accepted_deliverable_row.PhaseHint: Nonbinding: agree the affected operation/receiving contract before its dependent implementation and joined witness.

accepted_scope_rows.ScopeItemStatement: Route human and agent changes through the same host validation and application path with equivalent outcomes and errors.
Host domain truth and validation stay in the host's store and ownership.
Never present agent output as the host's accepted result without the host's recorded act.
Agent changes carry origin, conversation/workflow run and relied-on basis.
A change outside granted direct autonomy follows drafted, validated, queued, accepted and applied proposal states with receipt, or rejected, withdrawn or stale states.
Represent a proposal/application outcome that cannot be observed as unknown.
Refuse stale proposals with the reason and permit re-drafting on the current basis.
Never retarget a proposal because the selection later changes.
Repeated submission of the same proposal has only one effect.
Show proposal old/new values, affected objects and reasons in host views.
Operation success means execution and does not imply human acceptance.
Report a submitted proposal as queued until the host records acceptance and application.

CustomInstructions: Distinguish actual reserved human acts from routine operation permissions. Do not invent blanket approval or classifier policy. Host owns its validation/application/receipts/UI and domain truth; App/shared owner supplies receiving contract/fixtures. Names of upstream actors or schema concepts do not imply implementation ownership. Ground definitions in accepted source evidence; read relevant seed clauses through SourceRef and accepted companion files, not just names. Retain unresolved details explicitly at their point of need; do not require those decisions merely to write an honest contract. Scope IDs assigned jointly to more than one deliverable must be qualified to this contribution, preserving named integration owners. Enumerate exclusions and cite claims naming each actual owning contribution. Requirements/ACs must state testable outcomes without inventing numbers/technical choices. Per matrix row, group ACs only if verification methods are identical; prefer oneACperrow. Upstream local IDs must be qualified. No full research sweep, current network/supplier experiments, provider/sibling source edits, underscore edits, Git mutations or delegation. Manager can authorize bounded repair of this unaccepted initialized draft without using a spurious amendment.
